chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yūsuf, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Bashīr, from Ḥukaym, the mu'adhdhin of Banū ʿAbs, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
His saying, Exalted is He: “And know that whatever thing you gain, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger.”
He said: By Allah, it is the gain that comes day by day, except that my father made our Shi'ah exempt from that, so that they may be purified.

key_terms.خُمُسَهُ: its one-fifth share owed as khums
key_terms.شِيعَتَنَا: our Shi'ah; the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.غَنِمْتُمْ: you gained or acquired; here, wealth or benefit obtained
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in a state of permissibility or exemption
key_terms.لِيَزْكُوا: so that they may be purified
key_terms.يَوْمًا بِيَوْمٍ: day by day; continuously occurring gains

ai.seo_question: Does the khums verse apply only to war booty, or also to everyday gains and benefits?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse of khums as applying to ongoing gains and benefits acquired by a person over time. It also states that the Imam’s father granted the Shi'ah dispensation regarding this, expressing a concern for their purification.
